_comment: Dates are taken from what the commentaries themselves state. Where a commentary does not date its text, the entry is 'unresolved' and stays undated - the ledger prints those in a separate bucket rather than ordering them on a guess. Resolving one means finding the date in the commentary (or writing it into the commentary from the source), not recalling it. Volume order is never a proxy for composition order.

entries.note: Two editions, twelve years apart. The commentary works from the B-text and marks the layers throughout: first-edition-only passages in smaller type (§7, part of §8), second-edition footnotes and the §10 Addendum as marginal self-corrections (the pure-ego recantations at §§6 and 8; the noesis/noema footnote at §16). A unit should carry the A- or B-stratum only where the commentary assigns the passage to one; otherwise leave it unset.

entries.note: The stratified entry that makes the rest of this file worth maintaining. Hua IV is not one date: a 1912 draft, Husserl's 1915 rework, two Stein copies, a Landgrebe typescript, and four years of Husserl's insertions into it. A unit extracted from Ideas II should carry the stratum it belongs to whenever the commentary assigns it one; dating the whole volume 1912 - or 1952, its publication - flattens exactly the development the ledger exists to show.
